SUMMARY: A Public Hearing considering a Transient Rental License and Coastal Development
Permit to allow renting or leasing of a room or rooms for periods of fewer than thirty (30)
consecutive days duration in the Multiple Residential – High Density (HD) zone at 311 Clarissa
Avenue. The Proposed Project is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality
Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15301 (Class 1 - Existing Facilities). The proposed
project is not located within the appealable area of the Coastal Zone.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S):

  1. Conduct a public hearing;

  2. Find this project exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant
  to Section 15301 under Class 1 (Existing Facilities) of the CEQA Guidelines, because it
  has no potential to have a significant effect on the environment; and

  3. Adopt Resolution No. PC 26-01 approving a Transient Rental License and Coastal
  Development Permit pursuant to PC#2904 (Attachment 1).

AUTHORIZING GUIDELINES: Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) Sections 3-1.309 and 9-8.103.a
authorize the Planning Commission to review and take action on applications for a Transient
Rental License and Coastal Development Permit.

BACKGROUND:

Application Information:

  Applicant  Lorena Villa Batarse and Charles Batarse
  Owner  Lorena Villa Batarse and Charles Batarse
  Location  311 Clarissa Avenue
  APN  7480-036-039
  General Plan  High Density Residential
  Land Use Designation
  Zoning Classification  Multiple Residential – High Density (HD)
  File Date  08/05/2025
   PC#2904 – 311 Clarissa Avenue
  Page 2

Existing Site and Area Context:

The project site is located on a regularly shaped parcel addressed 311 Clarissa Avenue. The
parcel is situated south of Beacon Street and north of Tremont Street. The lot is relatively flat,
with a gentle slope from west to east.

The project site is currently developed with a single-story single-family residence. The residential
building is one story, and consists of two bedrooms, two bathrooms, and a kitchen and living
area, totaling approximately 798 square feet. The unit is used as an owner vacation home. The
unit is to be rented as a single unit. Originally constructed in 1920, the residence has had several
subsequent additions.

All abutting properties are in the HD zone and represent a mix of one- and two-story residential
buildings. A vicinity map, including adjacent property types and existing short-term rental status,
is provided as Attachment 2 of this report.

Entitlement and Permit History:

There are no entitlements previously granted for the project site.

The site has three different permits for home improvement:

  •  Permit #19068 – Interior remodel and fire sprinklers (2019)
  •  Permit #20093 – Fire suppression system (2020)
  •  Permit #24091 – Remodel bathroom and kitchen plumbing and electrical (2024)
   PC#2904 – 311 Clarissa Avenue
  Page 3

PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The applicants, Lorena Villa Batarse and Charles Batarse, propose
to short-term rent a two-bedroom, two bathroom single-story single family residence, addressed
311 Clarissa Avenue. The building totals approximately 798 square feet in size. The maximum
occupancy of the unit will be six (6) individuals based on the bedroom count and license
limitations set forth in AMC Section 3-1.317.g.

The proposed rental floor plan is included in Attachment 3 of this report.

DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS: No issue items have been identified for the proposed project.
It is the opinion of Staff that existing regulations and standard conditions adequately address
potential nuisance concerns related to transient rental, and no additional conditions are required
to meet the findings necessary to grant the TRL for the property.

GENERAL PLAN, LAND USE, AND ZONING COMPLIANCE:

Pursuant to AMC Section 3-1.310 and 9-8.103.d, recommended findings for approval of a
Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit are provided in draft Resolution No.
PC 26-01 (Attachment 1).

Annual Growth Policy
The growth policy provides that new residential or commercial development should only be
permitted with confirmation from Southern California Edison Company (“SCE”) that adequate
fresh water is available. The project involves permitting short-term rental use of an existing
residential unit, with no modifications to the floor plan or bedroom count. Water demand for
residential buildings is calculated based on the number of bedrooms in the unit. Since the floor
plan of the unit is not impacted, the project is not subject to evaluation of an allocation for water
service. Therefore, staff recommends that the Planning Commission make the finding that the
proposed project is in compliance with the 2025 Annual Growth Policy.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION: The proposed project is categorically exempt from the
provisions of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines
15301 (Class 1 – Existing Facilities) because it has no potential to have a significant effect on the
environment.

The Class 1 exemption includes the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing,
licensing, or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical
equipment, or topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of use. The project
involves permitting short-term rental use for an existing residential unit, involving no expansion
of the residential use on the project site, in compliance with all operational regulations set for in
Avalon Municipal Code Chapter 3-1, Business Licensing, Article 3, Transient Rental Licenses.
As such, the project is not expected to have a significant environmental impact on the
surrounding area.

Furthermore, the project was evaluated pursuant to the criteria for the exceptions to the
exemptions as identified in Guidelines Section 14 CCR, Chapter 3, Article 19, Section 15300.2
and the Planning Commission finds that there are no exceptions to the use of an exemption for
the project. The project does not impact an environmental resource of hazardous or critical
concern, does not result in cumulative impacts, does not have a significant effect on the
   PC#2904 – 311 Clarissa Avenue

environment due to unusual circumstances, does not damage scenic resources within a state
scenic highway, is not a hazardous waste site, and is not identified as a historical resource.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: On January 9, 2026, the City sent a Public
Hearing Notice to owners/tenants within a 300-foot radius of the project site. The Hearing Notice
was published in Catalina Islander on January 9, 2026. The notice was posted at the project site
and in two additional locations on the same date.

DRAFT RESOLUTION NO. PC 26-01
   RESOLUTION NO. PC 26-01

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
  AVALON APPROVING A TRANSIENT RENTAL LICENSE AND
  COASTAL DEVELOPMENT PERMIT FOR AN EXISTING SINGLE-
  FAMILY RESIDENCE LOCATED AT 311 CLARISSA AVENUE (PC#2904)

  WHEREAS, Lorena Villa Batarse and Charles Batarse (“Applicant”) filed an application
(“Application”) for a Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit (PC#2904) to
allow renting or leasing of a room or rooms for periods of fewer than thirty (30) consecutive days
duration (“Project”) for the single-family residence located at 311 Clarissa Avenue, APN 7480-
036-039 (“Site”); and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission has authority per Avalon Municipal Code (AMC)
Sections 3-1.309 and 9-8.103.a to review and take action on the subject applications for a Transient
Rental License and a Coastal Development Permit; and

  WHEREAS, the Site is categorized High Density Residential by the General Plan Land
Use Element and is located within the designated area of the Multiple Family, High Density (HD)
zoning district as defined by AMC Section 9-5.406; and

  WHEREAS, the Site is located within the Coastal Zone and is within the planning
boundaries of the Avalon Local Coastal Program; and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission conducted one duly advertised public hearing on
January 21, 2026, at which time interested persons had an opportunity to testify either in support
of or opposition to granting a Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit upon
property described in attached Exhibit “A”; and

  WHEREAS, all other legal prerequisites for the approval of the Transient Rental License
and Coastal Development Permit have occurred.

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Planning Commission of the City of
Avalon does hereby approve a Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit to allow
renting or leasing of a room or rooms for periods of fewer than thirty (30) consecutive days
duration for the single-family residence located at 311 Clarissa Avenue, based on the following
findings:

SECTION 1 – ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The proposed project is categorically exempt from the provisions of the California Environmental
Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15301 (Class 1 – Existing Facilities) because it
has no potential to have a significant effect on the environment.
The Class 1 exemption includes the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing,
or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical equipment, or
topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of use. The project involves

  1
 permitting short-term rental use for an existing residential unit, involving no expansion of the
residential use on the project site, in compliance with all operational regulations set forth in Avalon
Municipal Code Chapter 3-1, Business Licensing, Article 3, Transient Rental Licenses. As such,
the project is not expected to have a significant environmental impact on the surrounding area.
Furthermore, the project was evaluated pursuant to the criteria for the exceptions to the exemptions
as identified in Guidelines Section 14 CCR, Chapter 3, Article 19, Section 15300.2 and the
Planning Commission finds that there are no exceptions to the use of an exemption for the project.
The project does not impact an environmental resource of hazardous or critical concern, does not
result in cumulative impacts, does not have a significant effect on the environment due to unusual
circumstances, does not damage scenic resources within a state scenic highway, is not a hazardous
waste site, and is not identified as a historical resource.

SECTION 2 – FINDINGS
Transient Rental License
The proposed project may be granted a Transient Rental License for short-term rental per AMC
Chapter 3-1 (Business Licensing) Article 3 (Transient Rental Licenses). AMC Section 3-1.310 sets
forth the required findings for approval of a Transient Rental License as follows:
  a) The Planning Commission may, with such conditions as are deemed necessary, approve a
  Transient Rental License which will not jeopardize, adversely affect, endanger or
  otherwise constitute a menace to the public health, safety or general welfare, or be
  materially detrimental to the property of other persons located in the vicinity of such use.
  Standard conditions of approval for all transient rentals, as set forth in AMC Section 3-1.317,
  have been incorporated into the approval of the project. No additional special conditions are
  required in order to ensure compliance with the transient rental license operational regulations.
  b) In making such determination, the Planning Commission shall find that the proposed
  transient rental use is in general accord with the following principles and standards:
  1)  The nature, condition, and development of adjacent uses, buildings and structures
  shall be considered and no proposed transient rental use shall be permitted where
  such use will adversely affect or be materially detrimental to said adjacent uses,
  buildings and structures;
  The subject property is an existing single-family residence located within a
  predominantly residential area of the Flats. No modifications to the property are
  proposed that would alter the ability of the building to function as a single-family
  residence in the future. The property was inspected by the Planning and Building
  Department prior to the public hearing, and no health and safety issues were
  identified by the inspector that would prevent the residence from being used as a
  transient rental. Standard conditions of approval ensure that the operation of the
  transient rental will remain orderly and not have an adverse effect on surrounding
  residential properties.

  2
   2)  The site for a proposed transient rental use shall be adequate in size and shape to
  accommodate the yards, walls, fences, parking and loading facilities, landscaping,
  outdoor entertaining areas and other development features prescribed in this
  chapter or as required as a condition in order to integrate said use and not be
  detrimental with the uses in the neighborhood;
  The subject property is an existing two bedroom, two bathroom single-family
  residence and includes a living and kitchen area, totaling approximately 798 square
  feet. Pursuant to standard Condition #5, the property shall not provide a vehicle for
  the use of transient guests.
  3)  The site for a proposed transient rental use shall be served by highways and streets
  adequate in width and improved as necessary to carry the kind and quantity of
  traffic such use would generate.
  The project site is located on the west side of Clarissa Avenue between Beacon
  Street to the north and Tremont Street to the south. One block to the east is
  Clemente Avenue and one block to the west is Descanso Avenue. This is a heavily
  traveled area by both vehicles and pedestrians, and the surrounding streets are
  identified as Major Circulation Facilities in the General Plan Circulation Element.
  It is anticipated that existing sidewalks and roadways, combined with the fact a
  vehicle will not be provided to transient guests, will ensure that traffic associated
  with operation of the business will not interfere with circulation along Clarissa
  Avenue.
  4)  That the transient rental use must be ancillary to the residential use of residential
  unit, and would not create a commercial use in a residential zone. Whether a use
  is for a commercial use may be determined by the number of transient rental
  licenses previously granted to the applicant, the applicant's reason for the license
  and the nature of the requested license and any other factors presented in the
  application or at the hearing.
  The applicant currently does not operate any other transient rentals within the city.
  According to the owners, the property has been used as an owner-occupied vacation
  home. No modifications are proposed to the residence that would intensify the use
  of the property or alter the ability of the residence to function as a single-family
  residence in the future.
c) Conditions imposed by the Planning Commission for a Transient Rental License may
  involve any pertinent factors affecting the establishment, operation and maintenance of the
  requested transient rental use, including, but not limited to:
  1) Special yards, open spaces and buffer areas;
  2) Fences and walls;
  3) Parking facilities, including vehicular ingress and egress and the surfacing of parking
  area and driveways to specified standards;
  4) Street and highway dedications and improvements including sidewalks, curbs and
  gutters;
  5) Water supply and fire protection;

  3
   6) Landscaping and maintenance of grounds;
  7) Regulation of nuisance factors such as noise, vibrations, smoke, dust, dirt, odors, gases,
  noxious matter, heat, glare, electromagnetic disturbances and radiation;
  8) Regulation of operating hours for activities affecting normal neighborhood schedules
  and functions;
  9) Regulation of signs, including outdoor advertising; and
  10) Such other conditions as will make possible the development of the proposed transient
  rental use in an orderly and efficient manner and in general accord with all elements
  of the General Plan and the intent and purpose of this chapter.
  Standard conditions of approval for all transient rentals, as set forth in AMC Section 3-
  1.317, have been incorporated into the approval of the project. No additional special
  conditions are required in order to ensure compliance with the transient rental license
  operational regulations.
d) The Planning Commission shall deny the requested Transient Rental License where:
  1) The findings indicate, and the Commission determines, that the applicant has failed to
  show that the requested transient rental use will not jeopardize, adversely affect.
  endanger or otherwise constitute a menace to the public health, safety or general
  welfare or be materially detrimental to the property of other persons located in the
  vicinity of such use, and reasonable restrictions or conditions to license the
  establishment of the proposed use will not prevent detriment or menace as indicated.
  Pursuant to AMC Section 3-1.310.a-c, the required findings have been made to
  determine that the proposed transient rental will not jeopardize, adversely affect,
  endanger, or otherwise constitute a menace to the public health, safety, or general
  welfare or be materially detrimental to the property of other persons located in the
  vicinity of such use. Standard conditions of approval for all transient rentals, as set
  forth in AMC Section 3-1.317, have been incorporated into the approval of the project.
  No additional special conditions are required in order to ensure compliance with the
  transient rental license operational regulations.
  2) The applicant fails to attend the hearing of the Planning Commission in person or
  virtually, unless a valid excuse is provided.
  The applicant confirmed with Staff their intent to be in attendance at the public hearing
  prior to the publication of the meeting agenda.
  3) The applicant has previously had a Transient Rental License revoked for failure to
  maintain such license in good standing or for violation of the Municipal Code or any
  condition of the permit or had a conditional use permit revoked for violation of any
  requirement of this Municipal Code or violation of any condition of approval of the
  permit.
  The applicant has not had a business license, conditional use permit, or transient rental
  license for transient occupancy in the past, nor has any such license revoked for
  violations of the Municipal Code.

  4
   4) The applicant previously operated a transient rental without a Transient Rental
  License. In deciding whether to deny the Transient Rental License on this basis, the
  Planning Commission may determine, in its reasonable discretion, whether substantial
  evidence supports that the applicant was not acting in bad faith when engaging in an
  illegal transient rental operation based upon: (1) the length of time that the operator
  failed to obtain a valid transient rental, (2) the length of time between when the
  operator was notified of the illegal operation and the time when the operator applied
  for a license, (3) whether the operator immediately discontinued illegal transient rental
  operation upon notice, (4) whether only one transient rental unit was operated, and (5)
  whether the operator was a sophisticated party, meaning the operator or its affiliates
  have engaged in transient rental operation previously. The applicant has the burden of
  presenting evidence that prior illegal transient rental operation was not conducted
  deliberately or in bad faith.
  The applicant has not previously operated a transient rental without a license within the
  city.
  5) The property proposed for transient rental use is out of compliance with any
  requirement of this Municipal Code at the time the Planning Commission hears the
  application.
  The project site is not subject to any active code enforcement cases and is otherwise in
  good standing with licensing and permitting requirements with the City of Avalon.
e) In addition to the foregoing, the Planning Commission shall consider the following in
  connection with an application for a Transient Rental License:
  1) Year-Round Rental Status. In the absence of adequate mitigating measures proposed
  by the applicant, the application should be denied where the subject property is or has
  been rented for periods of more than 30 consecutive days to the same occupant at any
  time during the two years preceding the application.
  Staff has found no evidence that the subject property has been rented for 30 or more

The subject unit has one exterior roof deck that will be accessible to transient renters. Exterior

take advantage of the sweeping views of the coastline in the area. Nuisance noise is generally
a concern for residents of any residential area. The applicable roof deck in the area of the hills
has potential for sound to travel due to the geography of the development.

The property is located within Noise District 1. This is the district assignment for residential or
other areas not depicted on AMC Section 5-13.04 Table 2. AMC Section 5-13.08.a.1.a prohibits
the operation or cause of operation of any radio receiving set, musical instrument, sound
amplifying equipment, television set, or any other machine or device which produces or
reproduces sound between the hours of 8:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m. in such a manner as to be
plainly audible from the real property line of which sound amplifying equipment is located absent
approval of a Special Use Permit.

AMC 3-1.317 provides standard conditions which are applicable to all transient rental and
incorporated into the draft resolution. Two conditions prohibit the use of unenclosed balconies,

SECTION 1 – ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The proposed project is categorically exempt from the provisions of the California Environmental
Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15332 (Class 32 – In-fill Development Projects)
because it has no potential to have a significant effect on the environment.

  1
 The Class 32 reflects a determination by the California Office of Planning and Research (OPR)
that projects that meet the Class 32 criteria will not have a significant environmental effect and,
therefore, are exempt from CEQA. (Berkeley Hillside Preservation v. City of Berkeley (2015) 60
Cal.4th 1086, 1102.) To apply, a project must be an in-fill development and meet the following
criteria: (1) is consistent with the applicable General Plan designation and applicable policies, as
well as applicable zoning designations and regulations, (2) would occur on a site less than five (5)
acres, (3) the project site must have no habitat value, (4) the project would not result in significant
traffic, noise, air quality, or water quality effects, and (5) the site can be adequately served by all
required utilities and public services. The Class 32 exemption reflects the understanding that “the
majority of private projects for which a government permit or similar entitlement is necessary are
minor in scope … and hence, in the absence of unusual circumstances, have little or no effect on
the public environment.” (Pacific Palisades Residents Association, Inc. v. City of Los Angeles
(2023) 88 Cal.App.5th 1338, 1363.) If a project meets the criteria and qualifies for the Class 32
exemption, the project is categorically exempt from CEQA unless one of the exceptions to
exemptions apply. The exemption is not limited to any use type and may apply to residential,
commercial, industrial, public facility, and/or mixed-use projects.

The project meets all of the aforementioned requirements and is exempt under Class 32, as
supported by substantial evidence:

  a) General Plan and Zoning Consistency: The project site is designated Special Commercial
  (SC) by the General Plan Land Use Element and is located within the SC Zoning District.
  The SC zoning designation provides an area in which both small scale residential and
  neighborhood retail and services can coexist harmoniously. Hotels and residential uses are
  permitted in the SC with approval of a Conditional Use Permit.
  b) Less Than 5 Acres: The project site is approximately 2,375 square feet (0.05 acres), which
  is less than five acres.
  c) No Habitat Value: The project site is located in an urban area currently developed with a
  single-family residence. Because of the existing site’s developed nature in a highly urban
  environment the site has no value as habitat for endangered, rare, or threatened species.
  There is no sensitive vegetation or habitat on-site. The project would not encroach into any
  jurisdictional waters or areas that support native and/or sensitive habitat. The property does
  not contain any wetland areas.
  d) No Significant Traffic, Noise, Air Quality or Water Quality Effects: Technical studies have
  been prepared that analyze the potential impacts of the proposed project on the surrounding
  community related to traffic, noise, and air quality. These studies conclude that the project
  will not generate a significant number of new vehicle trips, increase the ambient noise
  levels by more than 3 decibels, or generate construction or operations related emissions
  beyond the thresholds adopted by the South Coast Air Quality Management District. The
  site is currently fully developed, and a non-priority Water Quality Management Plan will
  be required to be prepared at the time of grading permit review.
  e) Utilities and Public Services: Access to all required utilities, including sewer, water,
  energy, are available at the project site. All public services, including police and fire
  protection, are adequate to accommodate the project. As conditioned and designed, the
  project will be adequately served by all required utilities and public services.

Annual Growth Policy:

City of Avalon has adopted an Annual Growth Policy to balance the demands of residential and
commercial development within the city limits with the availability of freshwater resources to
support community growth. The 2025 Annual Growth Policy provides that new commercial
development will only be permitted in compliance with the goals of the growth policy and with
confirmation in writing from Southern California Edison Company (“SCE”) that adequate fresh
water is available.
The project involves permitting a commercial business which requires an allocation for water
service. At the time of publication of the agenda, SCE has provided a water allocation letter for
Phase 1 of the project, inclusive of up to three (3) rooms/units of water based on the number of
bedrooms in the existing single-family residence on the project site.
However, in considering the project scope of work, the Planning Commission has determined that
the inclusion of a pool on the roof of the building is not consistent with the intent of the growth
policy, as the water allocation required for a pool will take away from the availability of fresh
water for other residential or commercial development necessary to support the community.
Therefore, the Planning Commission finds the project consistent with the 2025 Annual Growth
Policy with the inclusion of Condition #25 of this resolution, which requires that timing of permits
for Phase 1 correspond with the phasing plan, confirmation of a water allocation for Phase 2 prior
to issuance of any permits for improvements in that phase of site development, and that no pool
shall be included in the scope of the approved project.

Variance:

AMC Chapter 9-8.405 sets forth the required findings for approval of a Variance as follows:

  1. Variances from the terms of the Zoning Ordinance shall be granted only when,
  because of special circumstances applicable to the property including size, shape,
  topography, location or surroundings, the strict application of the Zoning Ordinance

  under identical zoning classification.

  The urban fabric of Avalon is relatively compact, with approximately 80-90 acres of
  existing development already located within the valley floor and the immediately
  surrounding hillsides. Individually owned lots in Avalon comprise less than 1% of the total
  city acreage. Therefore, it is important to maximize the use of land within the city within
  the development parameters of each zoning district, so long as it is consistent with overall
  community character.

  The applicant is requesting multiple variances from the development standards for the SC
  zone, as follows:

  6
   •  Allow building height of 18 to 30 ft above grade to top of parapet, with an
  additional 10 ft for rooftop bathroom enclosure, 12 feet for elevator tower, and
  16 feet for emergency staircase, where 28 feet is allowed.
  •  Allow 93% lot coverage, where a maximum of 80% is allowed.
  •  Allow 166% floor area, where a maximum of 140% is allowed.

  Though the property is of regular size, the sloped topography of the lot is unusual compared
  to the majority of other properties within the SC zone. The majority of lots within the
  Special Commercial zone, and commercial zoning districts in general, are located within
  the “Flats.” As a result, the development standards have been written to apply to lots with
  flat topography. For instance, the maximum building height in the SC zone is 28 feet. The
  municipal code definition for building height is “…the vertical distance from the lot's
  natural surface to the highest point of the building.” (AMC Section 9-3.608). Other zones
  in the c0ity, particularly the residential zones, have additional detailed standards for
  measurement of building height (low slope, hillside, steep hillside) that account for the
  topography present within the zone to allow for equitable development of all lots. However,
  in the case of a sloped lot in the SC zone, strict application of the definition of building
  height would mean that the actual buildable area of the lot would be substantially less on a
  sloped lot than a flat lot, which would deprive the property of the same development
  potential compared to other properties within the same zone.

  Therefore, the proposed variances may be granted in conformance with the findings of the
  municipal code, as there are special circumstances related to lot topography that would
  otherwise deprive the property of the development potential of other lots within the same
  zone that lack the sloped topography of this lot.

  interfere with circulation at the corner of Metropole Avenue and Beacon Street, which is a

  The project site is located in an area with access to all necessary utilities and services to
  support the proposed use, including electric, water, gas, sewer, saltwater, and internet.

  8.103.d.1)

  applicable.

  implements the following General Plan Goals and Policies: Policies II-8, II-12, II-20
  and II-21 of the Land Use Element.

  •  California Coastal Act: The proposed project complies with the following sections of
  the Coastal Act:

  Section 30250:

  “(a) New residential, commercial, or industrial development, except as otherwise
  provided in this division, shall be located within, contiguous with, or in close proximity
  to, existing developed areas able to accommodate it or, where such areas are not able
  to accommodate it, in other areas with adequate public services and where it will not
  have significant adverse effects, either individually or cumulatively, on coastal
  resources. In addition, land divisions, other than leases for agricultural uses, outside
  existing developed areas shall be permitted only where 50 percent of the usable parcels
  in the area have been developed and the created parcels would be no smaller than the
  average size of surrounding parcels.”

  The project site is located within the urban center of Avalon, on an existing developed
  parcel surrounded by other commercial, institutional, and residential uses. The project
  site is adjacent to the intersection Metropole Avenue and Beacon Street public rights-
  of-way and is adequately served by all necessary utilities in order for the proposed use

  Section 30251:

  “The scenic and visual qualities of coastal areas shall be considered and protected as
  a resource of public importance. Permitted development shall be sited and designed to
  protect views to and along the ocean and scenic coastal areas, to minimize the
  alteration of natural land forms, to be visually compatible with the character of
  surrounding areas, and, where feasible, to restore and enhance visual quality in
  visually degraded areas. New development in highly scenic areas such as those
  designated in the California Coastline Preservation and Recreation Plan prepared by
  the Department of Parks and Recreation and by local government shall be subordinate
  to the character of its setting.”

  The project site is located within the city center of Avalon, on an urbanized parcel that
